limitsWhy.claudeMdLines: The Claude Code documentation's target: files over 200 lines consume more context and may reduce adherence.
limitsWhy.ruleLines: A rules file is read like a CLAUDE.md; the same target keeps each one readable whole.
limitsWhy.ruleChars: A scoped rule loads on demand and is cut at 40,000 characters on a 200K context window; a file under that loads whole for everyone.
limitsWhy.areaChars: The scoped rules of one area load together when a file there is touched; 40,000 characters is about 10,000 tokens, a cost worth paying on every such turn, and not more.
limitsWhy.unscopedChars: Rules without paths load in every session, so they are the most expensive per character; 10,000 keeps them to the few that really apply everywhere.
limitsWhy.skillLines: The documentation's target for a SKILL.md; reference material goes in files beside it, loaded when needed.
limitsWhy.memoryIndexLines: Only the first 200 lines of MEMORY.md load at a session's start; a line past that is a memory the session never knows it has.
limitsWhy.memoryIndexBytes: Or the first 25 KB, whichever comes first.
limitsWhy.onDemandCutoffSmallWindow: A nested CLAUDE.md or a scoped rule is cut here on a 200K context window; Claude gets a note that it may read the rest, and usually does not.
limitsWhy.onDemandCutoffLargeWindow: The same cut on a 1M context window with current models.
limitsWhy.skippedFileBytes: A CLAUDE.md over 4 MiB is skipped entirely.

gateWhy.tokens: A pushed secret cannot be taken back, even after a later commit removes it; the patterns need a token's real length after the prefix so a fake prefix in a test does not stop a commit.
gateWhy.controlBytes: A bell or another control character survives a type check and breaks a terminal or a string.
gateWhy.byteOrderMark: A byte-order mark is invisible, passes the compilers, and breaks the first line of a file or a commit message.
gateWhy.lineEndings: A repository that is LF only keeps diffs honest; a carriage return in one line makes the whole file look changed. Set to any to allow both.
gateWhy.nonAscii: warn names characters outside ASCII without stopping the commit; refuse stops it, for a repository whose convention is ASCII only; ignore says nothing. acceptedCharacters lists the exceptions, as characters or as U+XXXX.
gateWhy.neverCommitList: Words that must never be committed, one regular expression per line, kept outside every repository so the repository itself never holds them; the gate reads the file when it exists and says nothing when it does not.

outsidePathsWhy: An instruction file that names a session's scratch folder, a temp folder, a home folder or a memory note by its file points at something no other contributor and no other machine can see.
